comment: Ground truth by construction (spec coherence-format-v0.md §7). Each scene was written against exactly the docs listed as direct; style.md governed the prose of every scene (contextual); everything else was ignored while writing (unrelated). Traps = docs mentioned or echoed in the scene without any semantic dependency.

scene-01.notes: Named character with sheet facts (grey eyes, compass, fear of deep water, glassblower father); dated event via arithmetic (Drowning 701, present 723, 'twenty-two years').

scene-02.notes: Named character with sheet facts (right-leg limp, raven Pitch, kelp tea, no alcohol, soldier past).

scene-03.notes: Depends on world rules 1-4 without stating any rule or naming any sheet character. Unnamed boy.

trap.detail: 'old Marcus' waves across the quay; no marcus.md fact is used.

scene-05.notes: Guild-law facts (grey sash, iron rod as costume, wave-mark on inner left wrist, exile on second offence, forty crowns, city walls) plus Elena facts (unlicensed binder, dry humour).

scene-06.notes: Timeline dependency is implicit arithmetic only: 'two years he had kept the light' (721), 'four springs since the fog lifted' (719), fleet burned same summer (719), drowned quarter 'twenty-two years gone' (701). No year numbers appear.

trap.detail: Lantern Guild banners are pure scenery; no charter-law fact is used.

scene-07.notes: World rules 2 and 4 (sleep price collected the following night; ozone-and-salt smell noticeable to bystanders).

scene-08.notes: Multi-direct. Marcus's Guild grumbling comes from marcus.md (distrusts the Guild), not guild-law.md — no charter-law fact is used.

scene-09.notes: All guild-law facts (wave-mark on inner left wrist, exile on second offence, grey sash + iron rod, ninth-bell curfew, forty-crown licence) used without stating any as law. Unnamed dockhand girl, deliberately not Elena.

trap.detail: 'the glassblower's daughter' appears as crowd scenery; no elena.md fact is used.

scene-10.notes: Timeline via arithmetic: fire 'four years now' (719), Charter 'eleven years since the signing' (712), the Drowning recalled by an elder (701).
